# NIRSpec APT Review Tools

**[APT_review.py](APT_review.py)** is the main script. It takes an APT proposal as input and produces a review report and optional plots generated by **[msa_coverage_plot.py](msa_coverage_plot.py)**, **[plot_dithers.py](plot_dithers.py)**, and **[grid_dithers.py](grid_dithers.py)**.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Environment**: Always run scripts from the `mos_trace` micromamba environment:
> ```bash
> micromamba run -n mos_trace python APT_review.py <program> [options]
> # or activate the environment:
> micromamba activate mos_trace
> ```
>
> **CLI Options Reference**:
> - `--trace [true|false|skip]`: Calculate spectral coverage using `mos_trace` (`--trace` or `--trace true`), skip trace calculation (`--trace false` / default), or skip regenerating existing trace tables (`--trace skip`).
> - `--noplots`: Skip MSA coverage plot generation.
> - `--plots`: Only generate MSA coverage plots.
> - `--dithers` / `-d`: Generate dither/nod plots.
> - `--obs` / `-i`: Review only specific observations (e.g. `--obs 7` or `--obs 1:1,2,7-10`).
> - `--exclude` / `-x`: Exclude specific observations from review.
> - `--shorts-only` / `-s`: Quick scan only reporting electrically shorted shutters.
> - `--combined [auto|always|never]`: Strategy for combined multi-pointing / multi-visit coverage plots.
> - `--open`: Open the most recent timestamped review directory.
> - `--new`: Force new retrieval/export from APT into a fresh timestamped directory.

and in ~/NIRSpec/reviews/ (where active review work and updates take place).

3. Run the script and check the results as warranted or if requested.

4. After every update, push changes to the repository unless explicitly asked not to. Follow instructions in **[GitCommit.md](GitCommit.md)**.
